argon2_acquire_timeout_s.description: Maximum seconds a password or OAuth client-secret hash or verification waits for one of the ``argon2_max_concurrency`` slots before failing with HTTP 503 and a ``Retry-After`` header.
argon2_acquire_timeout_s.title: Argon2 Acquire Timeout S

argon2_max_concurrency.description: Per-process cap on concurrent argon2id password and OAuth client-secret hashes and verifications across all surfaces. Each argon2id call allocates 64 MiB (``memory_cost=65536``), so the default of 4 bounds peak argon2 memory at 256 MiB per process. Calls beyond the cap wait up to ``argon2_acquire_timeout_s`` for a slot and then fail with HTTP 503 + ``Retry-After`` instead of allocating another 64 MiB buffer.
argon2_max_concurrency.title: Argon2 Max Concurrency

failed_login_lockout_seconds.description: How long a locked admin account stays locked before logins are accepted again.
failed_login_lockout_seconds.title: Failed Login Lockout Seconds

failed_login_lockout_threshold.description: Consecutive failed logins after which an admin account is locked.
failed_login_lockout_threshold.title: Failed Login Lockout Threshold

jwt_secret.description: HMAC secret that signs admin login JWTs. Required in production (empty or placeholder values are rejected at startup); in development an ephemeral per-process secret is generated when empty.
jwt_secret.title: Jwt Secret

jwt_ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime of one admin login JWT. ``POST /auth/refresh`` re-mints the token, so this bounds a single token, not the session.
jwt_ttl_seconds.title: Jwt Ttl Seconds

session_ttl_seconds.description: Absolute cap on a web session: refresh re-mints the login JWT only while ``now - auth_time`` stays inside this window, so a leaked token cannot be kept alive indefinitely. Must be >= ``jwt_ttl_seconds``.
session_ttl_seconds.title: Session Ttl Seconds

stream_recheck_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between re-verifications of an open ``GET /events/stream``: its credential, ``events:read`` / ``org:admin`` permission, and the scope of the events it delivers. Checks run only at a poll or page boundary, so a check happens at the first poll or page after the interval elapses; an idle stream polls every few seconds, so a value below its poll interval behaves as that interval. A disabled caller, a revoked or expired token, or a revoked permission ends the stream at that check; a narrower permission set narrows it. Permissions are those the credential carries: API keys and ``at_`` access tokens resolve them live (an ephemeral agent ``at_`` keeps the subset it was minted with). A login session JWT carries the set it was issued with, but removing any of a user's effective permissions revokes their login sessions, so a stream opened with one ends at that check. The stream re-verifies the token it was opened with, so a permission added to a user reaches a login-session stream once the client reconnects with a newer login JWT.
stream_recheck_seconds.title: Stream Recheck Seconds

pepper.description: HMAC key for stored invite-token hashes. Required in production (empty or placeholder values are rejected at startup); in development an ephemeral per-process value is generated when empty. Changing it invalidates every outstanding invite.
pepper.title: Pepper

ttl_days.description: Days an admin invite token stays redeemable after it is issued.
ttl_days.title: Ttl Days

access_ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime (seconds) of an OAuth access token issued by the auth surface.
access_ttl_seconds.title: Access Ttl Seconds

assertion_max_ttl_seconds.description: Furthest in the future (seconds) a JWT-Bearer client assertion's ``exp`` may be; assertions expiring later are rejected.
assertion_max_ttl_seconds.title: Assertion Max Ttl Seconds

auth_code_ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime (seconds) of an OAuth authorization code before it must be exchanged.
auth_code_ttl_seconds.title: Auth Code Ttl Seconds

canonical_base_url.description: Public origin of the auth surface (``scheme://host[:port]``, no path), used for the OIDC issuer, the JWT-Bearer assertion audience and the SPA login callback. Unset falls back to ``server.public_base_url``, then the request or bind origin. A value with a path breaks the OAuth well-known discovery routes.
canonical_base_url.title: Canonical Base Url

claim_ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime (seconds) of the agent-ownership claim token minted at agent registration. Has no effect unless a claim-token minter is installed; the default build mints none.
claim_ttl_seconds.title: Claim Ttl Seconds

id_signing.description: ES256 keys for signing OIDC ID tokens. The first entry signs; every entry is published in the JWKS, so append the next key and later move it first to rotate. The local-dev key is rejected in production.
id_signing.title: Id Signing

platform_clients.description: Static first-party OAuth clients that authenticate with PKCE only (no secret). When ``auth.canonical_base_url`` is set, the operator SPA (``jentic-one-spa``) is added automatically if not listed.
platform_clients.title: Platform Clients

rat_ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime (seconds) of the registration access token returned when an agent registers, which the agent uses to check its registration status.
rat_ttl_seconds.title: Rat Ttl Seconds

refresh_ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime (seconds, default 7 days) of an OAuth refresh token; each refresh rotates it and the new token gets a fresh lifetime.
refresh_ttl_seconds.title: Refresh Ttl Seconds

jobs_api_base_url.description: Public base URL of the admin API (e.g. ``https://api.example.com``), used for the links a broker returns for async and held executions (``/jobs/{id}``, ``/executions/holds/{id}``, the approval review page). Unset, they are relative to the broker's own origin (the review page link tries ``server.public_base_url`` first); set it when the broker runs without the admin surface.
jobs_api_base_url.title: Jobs Api Base Url

jwt_secret.description: HS256 shared secret for verifying self-contained JWTs at the broker (signature and ``exp`` only), for development and tests. Unset disables this path; ``jwt_verification.trusted_issuers`` takes precedence when set and is the production option.
jwt_secret.title: Jwt Secret

resolve_cache_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds the broker caches a token or API-key validation verdict (and a JWT caller's active status) in process. Bounds how long a revoked token or disabled agent keeps working on each broker; 0 disables the cache.
resolve_cache_ttl_seconds.title: Resolve Cache Ttl Seconds

rule_cache_max_entries.description: Maximum entries in each broker process's permission-rule cache, one per active (agent, credential) binding; least recently used entries are evicted first.
rule_cache_max_entries.title: Rule Cache Max Entries

rule_cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds the broker caches the permission rules of an (agent, credential) binding in process; a rule change reaches each broker within this long. 0 disables the cache.
rule_cache_ttl_s.title: Rule Cache Ttl S

server_timing.description: Emit a W3C ``Server-Timing`` header on execute responses with per-stage durations (``jentic-auth``, ``jentic-egress``, ``jentic-discover``, ``jentic-rules``, ``jentic-body``, ``jentic-idempotency``, ``jentic-cred``, ``jentic-upstream``, ``jentic-persist``, ``jentic-total``) for authenticated callers. A broker-generated error raised before the upstream call lists the stages that ran without durations. ``jentic-upstream`` includes the circuit-breaker check, so a circuit-open ``503`` carries durations even though no upstream request was sent. Off by default: timing data aids side-channel probing and fingerprinting, so enable it only where callers are trusted with it (e.g. while diagnosing latency). Streaming responses carry only the stages known before the headers are sent (no ``jentic-persist``).
server_timing.title: Server Timing

streaming_persist_acquire_timeout_s.description: How long (seconds) a streaming execution persist waits for one of the ``broker.streaming_persist_max_concurrency`` slots. Past it the record is abandoned: logged as ``streaming_execution_persist_abandoned`` and counted on ``broker.streaming_execution.persist_failures`` (``reason=backlog_timeout``). The wait runs after the response is complete or the client has disconnected, when the request no longer holds its admission slot, so the wait delays neither the client nor ``/ready``. The timeout bounds how long a stalled admin database can keep records queued in memory, including at shutdown; it does not bound the write itself once a slot is held.
streaming_persist_acquire_timeout_s.title: Streaming Persist Acquire Timeout S

streaming_persist_max_concurrency.description: Per-process cap on concurrent post-response persists of streaming execution records (each holds one admin-DB connection). Excess persists wait for a slot, up to ``broker.streaming_persist_acquire_timeout_s``; the waiting and writing counts are exported as ``broker.streaming_execution.persist_pending``. The effective cap is clamped to ``databases.admin.pool_max - 1`` (minimum 1; a ``streaming_persist_limit_clamped`` warning is logged when it applies), so with ``pool_max >= 2`` persists never take every connection of the admin base pool. ``pool_max`` is the base pool size only; SQLAlchemy's default overflow can open up to 10 more connections on top of it.
streaming_persist_max_concurrency.title: Streaming Persist Max Concurrency

streaming_persist_timeout_s.description: Budget (seconds) for writing one streaming execution's record and lifecycle event. The write runs after the response, off the request, so it never delays the client; past the budget it is abandoned, logged and counted on ``app.background_tasks`` (``kind=streaming_execution_persist``, ``outcome=timed_out``).
streaming_persist_timeout_s.title: Streaming Persist Timeout S

toolkit_cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds the broker caches an agent's derived credential bindings in process. The cache is per instance, so a grant or revoke takes effect cluster-wide only once this lapses on every broker; 0 disables the cache.
toolkit_cache_ttl_s.title: Toolkit Cache Ttl S

upstream_timeout_s.description: Timeout (seconds) handed to the execution runner for one upstream call on the buffered sync path and the async job worker. Distinct from the transport-level ``broker.resilience.upstream`` timeouts and the ``request_deadline_s`` envelope.
upstream_timeout_s.title: Upstream Timeout S

BrokerResilienceConfig.description:
Resilience envelope: admission + rate limit / circuit.

The rate limiter and circuit breaker run on the process's shared-state
backend (the top-level ``state:`` section). Queue backpressure /
async-credential / retention knobs are future work.

max_in_flight.description: Hard admission cap on concurrently executing brokered calls, **per broker process** — replicas multiply it. At the cap, new requests are shed with 503 + ``Retry-After: shed_retry_after_s``.
max_in_flight.title: Max In Flight

readiness_saturation_threshold.description: Fraction of ``max_in_flight`` at/above which ``/ready`` reports unready, so the LB drains this instance before it hits the hard admission shed wall. Kept < 1.0 for that headroom.
readiness_saturation_threshold.title: Readiness Saturation Threshold

request_deadline_s.description: Overall wall-clock budget (seconds) for one upstream call, enforced by the always-on DeadlineRunner outside the circuit breaker — distinct from the per-attempt connect/read timeout on the transport client. Exceeding it returns 504 with a ``wait`` agent directive; 0 disables the budget. Size ABOVE upstream read timeouts so a single healthy slow attempt isn't pre-empted by the envelope deadline.
request_deadline_s.title: Request Deadline S

shed_retry_after_s.description: ``Retry-After`` (seconds) returned with the 503 when admission sheds at ``max_in_flight``.
shed_retry_after_s.title: Shed Retry After S

BrokerResilienceConfig.title: BrokerResilienceConfig

CatalogConfig.description: Public API catalog settings (manifest source + staleness).

manifest_max_age_seconds.description: Age (seconds) after which the cached catalog manifest is refreshed on the next catalog read. 0 disables automatic refresh (only ``POST /catalog:refresh``).
manifest_max_age_seconds.title: Manifest Max Age Seconds

manifest_url.description: Manifest source for the public API catalog. Full default: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jentic/jentic-public-apis/main/apis/openapi/apis.json
manifest_url.title: Manifest Url

preview_cache_failure_ttl_seconds.description: How long a failed catalog preview fetch (upstream unavailable, oversized or unparseable spec) is remembered per spec URL before it is retried, so repeated previews of a broken spec do not refetch it on every request. Zero retries on the next request. Ignored when the preview cache is disabled.
preview_cache_failure_ttl_seconds.title: Preview Cache Failure Ttl Seconds

preview_cache_max_entries.description: Maximum number of catalog spec projections held in memory per process (least recently used evicted first). Zero disables the cache.
preview_cache_max_entries.title: Preview Cache Max Entries

preview_cache_ttl_seconds.description: How long a catalog preview's upstream spec projection is reused before refetching. Zero disables the cache. The cache is per process: `POST /catalog:refresh` clears it only on the process that serves the refresh, so other workers or replicas can serve the previous projection until this TTL expires.
preview_cache_ttl_seconds.title: Preview Cache Ttl Seconds

update_check_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between update-check sweeps, which conditionally re-fetch the spec URLs of upstream-tracked APIs and emit ``catalog.update_available`` when an upstream spec changed; each API is probed at most once per interval. ``POST /catalog:refresh`` also triggers a sweep. 0 disables the check entirely (no events, no egress).
update_check_interval_seconds.title: Update Check Interval Seconds

update_sweep_deadline_seconds.description: Wall-clock budget (seconds) for one update-check sweep; it stops when exceeded.
update_sweep_deadline_seconds.title: Update Sweep Deadline Seconds

update_sweep_jitter_ratio.description: Random extra delay added to each sweep interval, as a fraction of it (next sweep after ``interval * (1 + uniform(0, ratio))``), so replicas started together drift apart. 0 disables jitter.
update_sweep_jitter_ratio.title: Update Sweep Jitter Ratio

update_sweep_max_concurrency.description: Maximum concurrent spec probes in one update-check sweep. Keep it below the registry database pool size so sweeps never starve request traffic.
update_sweep_max_concurrency.title: Update Sweep Max Concurrency

CatalogConfig.title: CatalogConfig

CircuitBreakerConfig.description:
Per-upstream circuit breaker.

Counts failures/totals per rolling ``window_s`` on the shared-state
backend's atomic counters; when the failure ratio crosses
``failure_ratio`` the circuit opens (a ``set_if_absent`` latch) and
fast-fails for ``cooldown_s``. ``observation`` mode tracks + emits
``would_block`` but still calls the upstream (safe-rollout dry run).

cooldown_s.description: Seconds an open circuit fast-fails calls before the upstream is tried again.
cooldown_s.title: Cooldown S

enabled.description: Track upstream failures per host and fast-fail calls to a host whose circuit is open (5xx responses and transport errors count as failures).
enabled.title: Enabled

enforcement_mode.description: ``blocking`` fast-fails calls while the circuit is open; ``observation`` still calls the upstream and only counts ``circuit_would_block_total``, to validate thresholds before blocking.
enforcement_mode.title: Enforcement Mode

failure_ratio.description: Failure fraction within ``window_s`` at which the circuit opens.
failure_ratio.title: Failure Ratio

min_calls.description: Minimum calls in the window before the failure ratio can open the circuit, so a single early failure does not trip it.
min_calls.title: Min Calls

window_s.description: Rolling window (seconds) over which failures and totals are counted.
window_s.title: Window S

CircuitBreakerConfig.title: CircuitBreakerConfig

ConnectConfig.description: Configuration for the OAuth connect flow.

state_secret.description: Key that signs the OAuth connect ``state`` parameter. Required in production (empty or placeholder values are rejected at startup); in development an ephemeral per-process value is generated when empty.
state_secret.title: State Secret

state_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds a signed connect ``state`` (and its browser-binding cookie) stays valid, i.e. how long a user has to finish the provider's consent screen.
state_ttl_seconds.title: State Ttl Seconds

ConnectConfig.title: ConnectConfig

ControlConnectConfig.description: Agent connect-session settings on the control surface.

manual_flows_enabled.description: Allow connect sessions that target a registry API (rather than a vendor-registry key), where a human enters the credential, or brings an OAuth app, when approving them in the dashboard. On by default; while off, `:connect` refuses API targets with `manual_flows_disabled`.
manual_flows_enabled.title: Manual Flows Enabled

manual_flows_ttl_hours.description: Hours an API-target connect session (a human-entered credential, or an OAuth API waiting for an app) stays open before it expires. Vendor OAuth sessions keep their fixed 30-minute lifetime.
manual_flows_ttl_hours.title: Manual Flows Ttl Hours

max_open_sessions_per_agent.description: Most open connect sessions one agent may hold at once while `manual_flows_enabled` is on; one more `:connect` gets 429 `too_many_open_sessions`.
max_open_sessions_per_agent.title: Max Open Sessions Per Agent

max_open_sessions_per_owner.description: Most open connect sessions across one user and the agents they own while `manual_flows_enabled` is on; one more `:connect` gets 429 `too_many_open_sessions`.
max_open_sessions_per_owner.title: Max Open Sessions Per Owner

rejection_cooldown_hours.description: Hours after a human rejects an agent's connect or access-change request during which the agent's repeat ask for the same target (or binding) gets 429 `recently_rejected`. Off (0) by default: an agent may ask again at once.
rejection_cooldown_hours.title: Rejection Cooldown Hours

ControlConnectConfig.title: ControlConnectConfig

ControlEgressConfig.description:
Private-network allowlist for the platform's OAuth and credential calls.

Holds only the two allowlist keys. A key left unset takes its value from
the matching ``broker.egress`` key. These calls always pin DNS, so there is
no ``dns_pinning_enabled`` key here, and unknown keys are rejected.

allowed_internal_domains.description: Domain suffixes (e.g. ``[".corp.internal"]``) whose resolved private IP is permitted for these calls; unset inherits `broker.egress.allowed_internal_domains`. The resolved IP must still fall in an allowed subnet. Accepts a YAML list or a comma-separated string.
allowed_internal_domains.title: Allowed Internal Domains

allowed_private_subnets.description: CIDRs exempted from the private-IP block for these calls (e.g. ``["10.50.0.0/16"]``); unset inherits `broker.egress.allowed_private_subnets`, and `[]` blocks every private range for these calls even when the broker allows one. The cloud-metadata and platform-credential IPs are never exempted. Accepts a YAML list or a comma-separated string.
allowed_private_subnets.title: Allowed Private Subnets

ControlEgressConfig.title: ControlEgressConfig

ControlSurfaceConfig.description:
Control surface configuration.

``egress`` is the allowlist for the platform's outbound OAuth and credential
calls. Each ``control.egress`` key left unset takes its value from the
matching ``broker.egress`` key. The policy is read by whichever process makes
the call: the control surface for credential and OAuth app writes, the
connect-session confirm, code exchange, device authorization and the
identity probe, and the broker surface for the token refresh it runs before
injecting a credential. With one process per surface, set ``control.egress``
(and the ``broker.egress`` keys it inherits) identically on both.

Unknown subkeys of ``control:`` are ignored, so a section written for
another release keeps validating; ``control.egress`` rejects unknown keys so
a mistyped allowlist key fails at startup instead of silently allowing less.

egress.description: Private-network allowlist for the platform's OAuth and credential calls: OAuth2 credential and OAuth app registration URL checks, own-client endpoints confirmed on a connect session, token exchange and refresh, device authorization, and the vendor identity probe. Each key left unset takes its value from `broker.egress`; set a key (e.g. `allowed_private_subnets: []`) to override it for these calls alone. These calls always pin DNS. The process making the call reads it, and the broker surface makes token refresh calls, so with one process per surface set it identically on the control and broker surfaces.

ControlSurfaceConfig.title: ControlSurfaceConfig

providers.description: Credential providers keyed by provider id, which credentials name in their ``provider`` field; ``kind`` selects the provider type. The built-in ``static`` and ``device_authorization`` providers are always present, and the connect flow uses the ``direct_oauth2`` entry.
providers.title: Providers

DatabaseConfig.description:
Connection parameters for a single database.

Supports two backends:

- ``postgres`` (default): uses host/port/user/password/name + schema_name.
- ``sqlite``: uses ``path`` (a single-file database). The Postgres
  connection fields are ignored.

backend.description: Database engine for this connection: ``postgres`` uses the server connection fields; ``sqlite`` uses ``path`` and ignores them.
backend.title: Backend

busy_timeout_ms.description: SQLite: per-connection wait for a held write lock, in milliseconds, before failing with ``database is locked``.
busy_timeout_ms.title: Busy Timeout Ms

journal_mode.description: SQLite journal mode (persistent per database file). ``WAL`` lets a writer and readers proceed concurrently instead of blocking each other.
journal_mode.title: Journal Mode

name.description: PostgreSQL database name. Required for the ``postgres`` backend.
name.title: Name

path.description: SQLite: filesystem path to the database file (``:memory:`` for in-memory). Required for the ``sqlite`` backend.
path.title: Path

pool_max.description: Maximum connections in the PostgreSQL connection pool (ignored for SQLite).
pool_max.title: Pool Max

pool_pre_ping.description: PostgreSQL: test pooled connections on checkout and transparently replace a dead one. By default the wire ping (three round trips on asyncpg: ``BEGIN``, ``;``, ``ROLLBACK``) runs only when the connection has sat idle in the pool for at least ``pool_pre_ping_idle_s`` seconds; active checkouts within that window skip the wire ping unless the driver connection is already closed. With ``false``, ``pool_recycle_s`` and TCP keepalive do not cover a Postgres restart or failover, a pooler/proxy restart, or a terminated backend: after such an event the first request on each pool per process can fail with an HTTP 503 (work run through the retrying transaction helper is re-run on a fresh connection instead). Only disable it where those events are rare and that error is acceptable. Ignored for SQLite.
pool_pre_ping.title: Pool Pre Ping

pool_pre_ping_idle_s.description: PostgreSQL: seconds a connection must sit idle in the pool before checkout runs the ``pool_pre_ping`` wire check. Active checkouts returning within this window skip the wire ping unless the driver connection is already closed. ``0`` pings on every checkout. Only applies when ``pool_pre_ping`` is ``true``. Ignored for SQLite.
pool_pre_ping_idle_s.title: Pool Pre Ping Idle S

pool_recycle_s.description: PostgreSQL: replace a pooled connection once it is this many seconds old, on its next checkout, so a connection silently dropped by a middlebox or left behind by a server restart is retired before use. Keep it below any server, proxy, or NAT idle timeout on the path. ``0`` disables recycling. Ignored for SQLite.
pool_recycle_s.title: Pool Recycle S

schema_name.description: PostgreSQL schema for this connection: created if missing by the migration runner (``CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS``) and put first on ``search_path``, so several connections can share one database.
schema_name.title: Schema Name

tcp_keepalive.description: PostgreSQL: enable TCP keepalive on each pooled connection's client socket so a peer that vanished while the connection sat idle is detected in about ``tcp_keepalive_idle_s + tcp_keepalive_count * tcp_keepalive_interval_s`` seconds instead of the OS default of hours. ``false`` leaves the socket at the OS defaults. Ignored for SQLite.
tcp_keepalive.title: Tcp Keepalive

tcp_keepalive_count.description: PostgreSQL: unanswered TCP keepalive probes before the connection is declared dead (``TCP_KEEPCNT``). Only applies when ``tcp_keepalive`` is ``true``. Ignored for SQLite.
tcp_keepalive_count.title: Tcp Keepalive Count

tcp_keepalive_idle_s.description: PostgreSQL: seconds a connection may sit idle before the first TCP keepalive probe is sent (``TCP_KEEPIDLE``; ``TCP_KEEPALIVE`` on macOS). Only applies when ``tcp_keepalive`` is ``true``. Ignored for SQLite.
tcp_keepalive_idle_s.title: Tcp Keepalive Idle S

tcp_keepalive_interval_s.description: PostgreSQL: seconds between unanswered TCP keepalive probes (``TCP_KEEPINTVL``). Only applies when ``tcp_keepalive`` is ``true``. Ignored for SQLite.
tcp_keepalive_interval_s.title: Tcp Keepalive Interval S

DatabaseConfig.title: DatabaseConfig

DirectOAuth2ProviderConfig.description: Configuration for a direct OAuth2 provider.

authorize_extra_params.description: Extra query parameters appended to every authorize URL. The defaults force the consent screen and ask Google for a refresh token; for Microsoft, Okta or Auth0 add the ``offline_access`` scope to ``default_scopes`` instead. Keys that collide with the OAuth2 parameters the provider builds (``response_type``, ``client_id``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state``, ``scope``) override them and break the connect flow.
authorize_extra_params.title: Authorize Extra Params

default_scopes.description: Scopes requested on the authorize URL when a connect request names none.
default_scopes.title: Default Scopes

expiry_skew_seconds.description: How many seconds before an access token's real expiry the broker refreshes it. Applied at comparison time; the stored expiry is never shifted.
expiry_skew_seconds.title: Expiry Skew Seconds

redirect_uri.description: OAuth callback URL registered with the IdP. Unset, it is derived per request as ``{server.public_base_url or request origin}/credentials/oauth/callback``; set it only when the public origin differs from ``server.public_base_url`` (e.g. a proxy the app cannot see). Matched byte-for-byte by the IdP.
redirect_uri.title: Redirect Uri

DirectOAuth2ProviderConfig.title: DirectOAuth2ProviderConfig

EgressConfig.description:
Outbound SSRF/egress policy for upstream calls.

Defaults are **strict** (both lists empty): every private range and the
cloud-metadata host are blocked. The two allowlists exist because the
broker is frequently installed *inside* a corporate network to bridge to
internal/legacy APIs, where the default block is a false positive. Both are
opt-in, auditable operator decisions; the cloud-metadata IP is a **hard,
non-overridable** deny so a credential-stealing SSRF can never be
allowlisted by accident.

allowed_internal_domains.description: Domain suffixes (e.g. ``[".svc.cluster.local"]``) whose resolved private IP is permitted. The resolved IP must still fall in an allowed subnet. Accepts a YAML list or a comma-separated string.
allowed_internal_domains.title: Allowed Internal Domains

allowed_private_subnets.description: CIDRs exempted from the private-IP egress block (e.g. ``["10.50.0.0/16"]``). The cloud-metadata and platform-credential IPs (e.g. 169.254.169.254, 169.254.170.2, fd00:ec2::254, 100.100.100.200) are never exempted, even when a listed range covers them. Accepts a YAML list or a comma-separated string.
allowed_private_subnets.title: Allowed Private Subnets

dns_pinning_enabled.description: Pin the outbound connection to the IP validated at connect time, closing the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU between pre-request validation and the runner's own resolution. Disable only to debug egress issues.
dns_pinning_enabled.title: Dns Pinning Enabled

EgressConfig.title: EgressConfig

active_id.description: Id of the key that encrypts new values; must match an entry in ``entries``. Older keys stay usable for decryption, so rotate by adding a key and switching this id.
active_id.title: Active Id

entries.description: AES-256-GCM keys (32 bytes, base64) for credentials at rest. Every entry can decrypt; ids must be unique. Empty still boots, but credential writes and approval-gated executions then fail. Never remove a key that still has data encrypted under it.
entries.title: Entries

EncryptionKey.description:
A single named encryption key.

Key material comes from exactly ONE source:

- ``material``      — inline in the config (local dev / vault-templated files),
- ``material_env``  — the name of an environment variable holding the key,
- ``material_file`` — a regular file to read the key from (docker/k8s secret
  mounts, systemd ``LoadCredential`` paths). Pipes and ``/dev/fd`` sources
  are rejected: config may be validated more than once per process, and a
  source that cannot be re-read would hang or fail the second load.

``material_env``/``material_file`` are resolved once, at config load, into
``material`` — consumers keep reading ``resolved_material`` and never learn
where the bytes came from (the source field is cleared after resolution, so
a resolved key re-validates cleanly and never re-reads the environment or
the file). Resolution failures (unset variable, unreadable file, empty
value) fail validation loudly rather than booting a server that cannot
decrypt its own credentials.

id.description: Key id (``[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+``), stored as the prefix of every value encrypted with this key so it can be decrypted after rotation.
id.title: Id

EntitlementConfig.description:
AWS Marketplace license gate for the Marketplace-listed deployment.

Powers the entitlement checker (``integrations/aws_marketplace``): on
startup, and every ``refresh_interval_seconds`` after, the process asks
AWS whether this deployment's Marketplace subscription is still active, and
locks the HTTP surface (503, health excepted) when it definitively is not.
Defaults to **OFF**: a non-Marketplace install that omits this block wires
nothing and never makes an AWS call.

Failure posture: an *unreachable* or *erroring* AWS API is never grounds
for lockout by itself — the last definitive verdict holds for
``grace_period_seconds`` before the gate fails closed. Only an explicit
"not entitled" answer from AWS locks out immediately.

enabled.description: Gate the HTTP surface on an active AWS Marketplace subscription (503 except health checks when AWS reports the deployment is not entitled). Off makes no AWS calls.
enabled.title: Enabled

grace_period_seconds.description: How long (seconds) the last definitive verdict holds while the AWS API is unreachable or erroring, before the gate fails closed. An explicit "not entitled" answer locks out immediately.
grace_period_seconds.title: Grace Period Seconds

license_dimensions.description: Contract pricing only: entitlement dimension keys checked out from the buyer's license; every one must be granted. Accepts a YAML list or a comma-separated string.
license_dimensions.title: License Dimensions

license_sku.description: Contract pricing only: the Marketplace product ID from the portal (``CheckoutLicense`` ``ProductSKU``) — not the product code; the portal issues both. Required when ``pricing_model`` is ``contract``.
license_sku.title: License Sku

pricing_model.description: Which Marketplace API the check calls: ``contract`` uses License Manager ``CheckoutLicense`` (requires ``license_sku``); ``usage`` uses Metering Service ``RegisterUsage`` (hourly/usage pricing).
pricing_model.title: Pricing Model

product_code.description: Marketplace product code issued by the AWS Marketplace portal for the container product. Required when ``enabled``.
product_code.title: Product Code

refresh_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between entitlement re-checks after the one at startup.
refresh_interval_seconds.title: Refresh Interval Seconds

Require-approval holds: held execution jobs awaiting a human reviewer.

An execute call matching a permission rule with ``effect="require-approval"``
is enqueued as a ``held`` job with a ``pending`` approval; a reviewer (the
agent's owner or an ``org:admin``) approves or denies it, or it expires.

ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds

IdempotencyConfig.description:
``Idempotency-Key`` replay store.

Sync ``FULL``-mode replay over the shared-state ``AtomicStore`` (the
``state:`` backend). Two TTLs: a *short* ``pending_ttl_s`` claim
(sized to the request deadline + buffer, so a crash mid-flight frees the key
in seconds rather than the full replay window) promoted to the *long*
``ttl_s`` only once the response is stored. Responses over
``max_response_bytes`` are recorded without their body (replay still prevents
a duplicate side-effect; only byte-for-byte body replay is dropped).

Compliance modes (``metadata_only`` / kill-switch), ``require_for_mutations``,
async same-``job_id`` replay, and at-rest encryption are future work.

enabled.description: Honour the ``Idempotency-Key`` request header on broker executions: a repeat of a completed key replays the stored response instead of calling the upstream again. Off ignores the header.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_response_bytes.description: Largest response body (bytes) stored for byte-for-byte replay. Larger responses are recorded without their body: a replay still prevents the duplicate call but does not return the body.
max_response_bytes.title: Max Response Bytes

pending_ttl_s.description: Lifetime (seconds) of the in-flight claim on an ``Idempotency-Key``, so a broker killed mid-request frees the key within seconds. Size it just above ``broker.resilience.request_deadline_s``.
pending_ttl_s.title: Pending Ttl S

ttl_s.description: Replay window of a completed Idempotency-Key record, in seconds. Unset, it is 3600 (1 h) on the memory shared-state backend and 86400 (24 h) on any other backend. On memory, every record is held in process for this long, so the TTL divides the sustained idempotent request rate the idem budget can hold.
ttl_s.title: Ttl S

JwtVerificationConfig.description:
Hardened inbound-JWT verification for the broker edge.

When ``trusted_issuers`` is non-empty the broker verifies self-contained JWTs
against the issuers' published JWKS (asymmetric, key-rotation-aware) and
enforces ``iss`` (trusted set), ``aud`` (``audience``), and ``exp``/``nbf``
with ``leeway_s`` clock-skew. Empty (the default) leaves the asymmetric path
off — the legacy HS256 ``broker.jwt_secret`` path (dev/test) still applies.

audience.title: Audience

trusted_issuers.description: Identity providers whose self-contained JWTs the broker accepts, each verified against its published JWKS. When non-empty this takes precedence over ``broker.jwt_secret``; empty leaves the JWKS path off.
trusted_issuers.title: Trusted Issuers

LocalLoginConfig.description:
Local-account login form on the ``/authorize`` flow (no external IdP).

Default **off**: ``/authorize`` behaviour is byte-identical (including the
``server_error`` redirect when no IdP is configured) and ``GET|POST /login``
answer the framework's plain 404. Enabling it makes the standards-track
native-app sign-in flow (RFC 8252: DCR + system browser + loopback redirect
+ PKCE) work against the first-party password account store, without any
client ever handling a password. An external IdP always wins: when
``auth.idp.enabled`` is true the login form is never offered (no mixed
mode in v1).

enabled.description: Offer a first-party password login form on the /authorize flow. Off by default; when auth.idp.enabled is true the external IdP always wins and the form is never offered.

MemoryBackendConfig.description:
Bounds for the in-process (``memory``) shared-state backend.

Every key belongs to a namespace, its prefix up to the first ``:``
(``idem`` for Idempotency-Key records, ``idem-body`` for their stored
response bodies, ``auth`` for the auth surface's single-use markers,
``login-csrf`` for login CSRF nonces, ``cb`` for circuit-breaker counters
and their open-circuit report claims, ``broker-authfail`` and
``broker-authfail-emit`` for the broker's auth-failure counters,
``mcp-session`` and ``mcp-session-cap`` for the MCP session-event dedupe,
``repeated_failure`` for the broker's repeated-failure counters, and so
on). Each namespace has its own budget, so one key kind filling up
never starves another. A namespace that is full of live entries refuses
new writes (the request that needed it gets a 503) rather than evicting a
live entry; the telemetry namespaces (``broker-authfail*``, the ``cb``
report claims, ``mcp-session*``) only skip the count or fall back to the
database dedupe instead. Ignored by every other backend.

max_bytes_per_namespace.description: Default most approximate bytes (key + value + about 750 bytes of per-entry overhead) one key namespace may hold before its writes are refused.
max_bytes_per_namespace.title: Max Bytes Per Namespace

max_entries_per_namespace.description: Default most live entries one key namespace may hold before its writes are refused.
max_entries_per_namespace.title: Max Entries Per Namespace

max_total_bytes.description: Most approximate bytes all namespaces of the memory backend may hold together (201326592, 192 MiB, by default); a write past it is refused like a full namespace, never by evicting a live entry. A process builds one backend shared by every surface it serves, so this caps the whole process's shared state. Raise the container memory limit together with it.
max_total_bytes.title: Max Total Bytes

namespaces.description: Per-namespace budget overrides, keyed by namespace (the key prefix before the first ``:``). Unless overridden here, idem (Idempotency-Key records) is 250000 entries / 134217728 bytes (128 MiB) and idem-body (their stored response bodies) 1000000 entries / 33554432 bytes (32 MiB), each with a 0.1 per-caller share; login-csrf (login page CSRF nonces) uses max_entries_per_namespace / max_bytes_per_namespace with a 0.02 per-client share, about 370 live nonces per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 at the defaults (about 900 bytes each, 5-minute TTL), twice what the default authorize rate limit lets one client network request in that time; repeated_failure (the broker's repeated-failure counters, which gate the execution.repeated_failure database scan) is 10000 entries / 8780000 bytes (about 8.4 MiB), about 2500 concurrently failing actor + credential + operation keys, and fails open when full (every failure runs the scan); every other namespace uses max_entries_per_namespace / max_bytes_per_namespace. The sustained idempotent request rate idem can hold is min(max_entries, max_bytes / record_bytes) / broker.idempotency.ttl_s, where record_bytes is about 1000 bytes plus the response headers (capped at 512 bytes): about 30 req/s at the defaults and a 1 h TTL, and a tenth of that per caller. Above it, Idempotency-Key requests get 503 idempotency_unavailable; bodies (about 830 bytes + body length each) stop being stored for replay sooner, about 5 req/s of 1 KiB bodies, without refusing requests.
namespaces.title: Namespaces

MemoryBackendConfig.title: MemoryBackendConfig

MemoryNamespaceBudgetConfig.description: Entry-count and approximate byte budget for one memory-backend key namespace.

max_owner_share.description: Most of max_entries and max_bytes that one owner (the key's second ``:`` segment: for idem and idem-body the calling actor, for login-csrf the client's IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) may hold; an owner over its share is refused without affecting the others. Unset, it is 0.1 for idem and idem-body, 0.02 for login-csrf and unlimited elsewhere; 1.0 lets one owner use the whole namespace.
max_owner_share.title: Max Owner Share

approval_status_rpm.description: Sustained requests/minute allowed on the approval-pending status poll (``GET /oauth/approval/status``). Its own namespace, so polling can never drain the ``/authorize`` or registration quota: one pending tab polls at 12 rpm, so the default keeps ~10 concurrent pending tabs behind one NAT inside the bucket, and the page honors ``Retry-After`` with backoff, so saturation degrades to a slower cadence rather than a thundering retry.
approval_status_rpm.title: Approval Status Rpm

authorize_rpm.description: Sustained requests/minute allowed per client network (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) across the unauthenticated authorization flow: ``/authorize``, the IdP callback, the consent page, its submit and inline agent create, and the local-login form share one bucket, whatever ``client_id`` they name. A sign-in spends two to six requests (more after a mistyped password), so the defaults admit at least five back-to-back sign-ins and then at least five a minute per network; raise both for a large shared NAT or egress IP. Behind a proxy, set ``auth.oauth_rate_limit.trusted_proxies`` or every client shares the proxy's bucket.
authorize_rpm.title: Authorize Rpm

exchange_rpm.description: Sustained requests/minute allowed per ``client_id`` + client network (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) on the token endpoint (also reused per client network for token revocation).

registration_rpm.description: Sustained requests/minute allowed per client network (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) on anonymous dynamic client registration (``POST /oauth-clients``).
registration_rpm.title: Registration Rpm

trusted_proxies.description: Reverse proxies whose ``X-Forwarded-For`` header is honored when deriving the per-client rate-limit identity: IP addresses or CIDR networks (e.g. ``10.0.0.0/8``, ``fd00::/8``), matched against the socket address and each forwarded hop by network membership. Accepts a YAML list or a comma-separated string. Invalid entries fail config load. Empty (default) means the socket address is used as-is — behind a reverse proxy every request then carries the proxy's IP and all clients share one bucket, so list the proxy IPs or pod CIDR when deploying behind one. Only list ranges your proxies alone hold: any host inside a trusted network can choose its own rate-limit identity.
trusted_proxies.title: Trusted Proxies

ReleaseCheckConfig.description:
"Update available" check for the running jentic-one build itself.

Powers ``GET /system/version``: the backend asks GitHub for the newest
published release of ``repo`` and compares it against the running build so the
web console can surface an "update available" banner (and the user menu can
always show the current version). This covers *jentic-one's own* release;
``CatalogConfig`` tracks the public *API catalog* instead.

Runs only on a ``local`` backend (a self-hosted install the operator can
actually update); the hosted platform (``server.backend == "remote"``) skips
it. The result is cached in-process for ``cache_ttl_seconds`` (fetch-on-read,
no background job), so at most one GitHub request happens per TTL regardless
of how many clients poll. Every failure degrades to "latest unknown" (no
banner) rather than erroring — the version probe must never break the app.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds the latest-release lookup is cached in process (default 6 h), so at most one GitHub request is made per TTL. 0 disables the check entirely (air-gapped installs, no egress).
cache_ttl_seconds.title: Cache Ttl Seconds

enabled.description: Check GitHub for a newer jentic-one release so the web console can show an "update available" banner. Runs only when ``server.backend`` is ``local``.
enabled.title: Enabled

ReleaseCheckConfig.title: ReleaseCheckConfig

RetryConfig.description:
Idempotency-aware upstream retry.

The ``RetryRunner`` decorator retries a failed attempt **only** when it is
safe to do so: a connect-phase failure (no bytes on the wire) is retryable
for any method, while a post-send failure (read timeout, mirrored ``429``/
``503``) is retried only for idempotent HTTP methods — ``Idempotency-Key``
is broker-consumed and stripped from outbound headers, so a post-send
``POST`` or ``PATCH`` retry would double-spend (#1799).
Each attempt still flows through the circuit breaker (retry *outside*,
breaker *inside*); the whole loop is bounded by the request deadline.

base_backoff_s.description: Base delay (seconds) of the exponential backoff ``base_backoff_s * 2**(attempt-1)``, capped at ``max_backoff_s``, then fully jittered and clamped to the request deadline.
base_backoff_s.title: Base Backoff S

enabled.description: Retry failed upstream attempts when safe: connect failures for any method, post-send failures (read timeouts, ``retry_statuses``) only for idempotent HTTP methods. Bounded by the request deadline. Streamed executions are never retried, and streaming is the default synchronous path while ``broker.resilience.upstream.stream_passthrough_enabled`` is true.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_attempts.description: Total attempts including the first (3 = the initial call plus up to 2 retries).
max_attempts.title: Max Attempts

max_backoff_s.description: Cap (seconds) on one retry backoff before jitter.
max_backoff_s.title: Max Backoff S

retry_statuses.description: Upstream status codes treated as transient and retried; an upstream ``Retry-After`` on them is honoured, capped at the request deadline.
retry_statuses.title: Retry Statuses

RetryConfig.title: RetryConfig

debug.description: Render stdout logs with the human-readable console renderer instead of JSON lines. For local development.

log_level.description: Root log level: an uppercase Python level name such as ``DEBUG``, ``INFO`` or ``WARNING``.
log_level.title: Log Level

SearchConfig.description:
Search configuration.

The built-in mode is "lexical" (BM25 on SQLite, native full-text on
PostgreSQL). ``search_mode`` is validated against the registered
SearchStrategy set at resolve time (``resolve_strategy``), so an unknown mode
fails loudly with the available modes for the active dialect rather than at
config load. Additional modes (e.g. "semantic", "vector") can be registered
via ``register_strategy`` without editing this schema.

enabled.description: Build the lexical search text for operations at import time. APIs imported while this is off are not findable by lexical search until re-imported.
enabled.title: Enabled

search_enabled.description: Serve search queries. Off, search requests fail with a search-disabled error; indexing at import is controlled separately by ``enabled``.
search_enabled.title: Search Enabled

search_mode.description: Search strategy name, resolved per database dialect against the registered strategies. ``lexical`` (BM25 on SQLite, native full-text on PostgreSQL) is built in; an unknown mode fails on first use with the available modes listed.
search_mode.title: Search Mode

public_base_url.description: The public origin of this deployment (e.g. ``https://jentic.example.com``). Absolute URLs the app hands to external clients — the OAuth connect ``redirect_uri``, the OIDC issuer and JWT-Bearer audience, DCR ``registration_client_uri``, the SPA login callback, approval links — fall back to it when their own more specific key is unset. Unset, they derive from the incoming request's origin, or from the bind (``http://{host}:{port}``) when there is no request; set it when clients reach the app through a reverse proxy, ingress or port mapping.
public_base_url.title: Public Base Url

reload.description: Run uvicorn with auto-reload on code changes (development only). Ignored, with a warning, when the admin database is SQLite or the config comes from a one-shot source such as a pipe.
reload.title: Reload

background_task_drain_timeout_s.description: On shutdown, how long (seconds) the app waits for work requests handed off after their response (e.g. streaming execution records) before cancelling what is still running. Runs before the databases close; each cancelled task is logged and counted on ``app.background_tasks`` (``outcome=cancelled``).
background_task_drain_timeout_s.title: Background Task Drain Timeout S

SigningKeyConfig.description: A single ES256 signing key for ID token issuance.

kid.description: Key id published in the JWKS and stamped in the ``kid`` header of ID tokens signed with this key (``[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+``).
kid.title: Kid

private_key_pem.description: PEM-encoded EC P-256 private key used for ES256 signing.
private_key_pem.title: Private Key Pem

StateBackendConfig.description:
The process's shared-state backend (top-level ``state:`` section).

One backend per process holds the rate-limit buckets, circuit-breaker
counters, ``Idempotency-Key`` records, the auth surface's single-use
markers, the broker's auth-failure counters and the MCP session-event
dedupe of every surface the process serves.

backend.description: Name of the shared-state backend to build: ``memory`` (in-process, the default), ``redis`` (deprecated), or a name an extension registered with ``register_state_backend``. An unregistered name fails at startup with the list of registered names.
backend.title: Backend

options.description: Settings for a backend registered by an extension, passed to its builder unvalidated (the builder validates them). Ignored by the built-in memory and redis backends.
options.title: Options

redis_key_prefix.description: Prefix the deprecated ``redis`` backend puts on every key; set a per-environment value when deployments share one Redis.
redis_key_prefix.title: Redis Key Prefix

redis_url.description: Connection URL of the deprecated ``redis`` backend; required by it.
redis_url.title: Redis Url

StateBackendConfig.title: StateBackendConfig

TelemetryConfig.description:
Anonymous product-telemetry settings.

Defaults to **OFF**: an instance whose config omits this block (non-onboarded
or hand-rolled) sends nothing. The onboarding CLI writes ``enabled``
explicitly (a yes-default ``[Y]/n`` prompt), which is where the
on-by-default install experience comes from. ``instance_id`` seeds the
durable admin-DB identity row on first startup for opted-in instances.
``host_os`` is the operator's OS family, stamped by the CLI at install
time so a Docker-run instance reports the host's OS rather than the
container's; sent once per boot, on the ``instance_booted`` event.

enabled.description: Send anonymous product telemetry. Off when the block is omitted; the onboarding CLI writes it explicitly.
enabled.title: Enabled

host_os.description: Host OS family stamped by the onboarding CLI, so an instance running in Docker reports the operator's OS rather than the container's Linux. Unset falls back to runtime detection; unrecognised values are reported as ``other``. Sent once per boot, on the ``instance_booted`` event.
host_os.title: Host Os

instance_id.description: Opaque instance id reported with telemetry (at most 64 characters). When set it is authoritative and overwrites the id stored in the admin database; unset, a random UUID is generated on first startup and kept.
instance_id.title: Instance Id

TelemetryConfig.title: TelemetryConfig

exporter.description: Where spans go. ``none`` records no spans at all (every span is non-recording), while trace ids are still generated and propagated: an inbound ``traceparent`` is honoured, outbound requests carry ``traceparent``/``tracestate``, and execution records and logs keep their ``trace_id``. With ``none`` the outbound ``traceparent`` has the sampled flag unset (``-00``) even when the caller sent ``-01``, since this process records nothing.
exporter.title: Exporter

sample_ratio.description: Fraction of traces recorded and exported when ``exporter`` is ``otlp`` (1.0 records every trace). It caps every trace entering the process, including requests that arrive with a sampled ``traceparent`` (the CLI and MCP send one on every call), so a caller cannot force recording. A caller's unsampled ``traceparent`` stays unsampled. Ignored with ``exporter: none``, and overridden by the standard ``OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`` environment variable when that is set (a warning is logged if this field is not 1.0).
sample_ratio.title: Sample Ratio

TrustedIssuerConfig.description:
A single trusted token issuer (IdP) and where to fetch its public keys.

The verifier holds one JWKS client per issuer; an unknown ``kid`` triggers a
bounded re-fetch (key rotation picked up without a restart). ``algorithms``
is the per-issuer asymmetric allowlist — HMAC/``none`` are rejected here so an
issuer can't be downgraded to a symmetric/forgeable signature.

algorithms.description: Signature algorithms accepted from this issuer. Asymmetric only (RS*, ES*, PS*, EdDSA); HMAC and ``none`` are rejected at load.
algorithms.title: Algorithms

issuer.description: Expected ``iss`` claim of tokens from this issuer (exact match).
issuer.title: Issuer

jwks_url.description: URL of the issuer's published JWKS. Must be https:// when JENTIC_ENV=production; plain http:// is accepted outside production (local/CI stacks) and logs a warning at config load.
jwks_url.title: Jwks Url

TrustedIssuerConfig.title: TrustedIssuerConfig

UpstreamClientConfig.description:
Bounds for the single shared outbound ``httpx.AsyncClient``.

The timeouts are httpx semantics: ``read_timeout_s`` is the *between-bytes*
gap timeout (per read), **not** a whole-stream cap — a trickle that keeps
sending under the limit can hold a pool slot open. The overall transfer
deadline is owned by the response-streaming guard, not here.

connect_timeout_s.description: Timeout (seconds) for establishing an upstream connection.
connect_timeout_s.title: Connect Timeout S

http2.description: Negotiate HTTP/2 via ALPN, falling back to HTTP/1.1 when the upstream does not offer it. Some upstreams (APNs, certain CDNs) refuse 1.1; set false only to pin HTTP/1.1.
http2.title: Http2

max_connections.description: Maximum open upstream connections in the shared client pool.
max_connections.title: Max Connections

max_keepalive.description: Maximum idle keep-alive connections the shared pool retains.
max_keepalive.title: Max Keepalive

max_per_host.description: Maximum concurrent calls to one upstream host, so one slow upstream cannot drain the whole connection pool.
max_per_host.title: Max Per Host

max_request_bytes.description: Default cap (bytes) on an execute request body, for content types without an entry in ``max_request_bytes_by_type``; over it the broker answers 413.
max_request_bytes.title: Max Request Bytes

max_request_bytes_by_type.description: Per-Content-Type request-body caps (bytes), matched most specific first: exact type (``application/json``), then wildcard (``audio/*``), then ``max_request_bytes``. A missing or unknown type gets the default, never unbounded.
max_request_bytes_by_type.title: Max Request Bytes By Type

max_response_bytes.description: Cap (bytes) on an upstream response body, enforced while reading: the connection is aborted as soon as it is exceeded. 0 disables the cap (unbounded; not recommended).
max_response_bytes.title: Max Response Bytes

pool_timeout_s.description: How long (seconds) a call waits for a free connection from the shared pool before failing.
pool_timeout_s.title: Pool Timeout S

read_timeout_s.description: Per-read *between-bytes* gap timeout (seconds, httpx semantics) on upstream responses — not a whole-stream cap. Pairs with ``broker.resilience.request_deadline_s``, which must be sized above it so one healthy slow attempt isn't pre-empted by the envelope deadline.
read_timeout_s.title: Read Timeout S

stream_passthrough_enabled.description: Stream upstream responses straight through to the client instead of buffering them. Applies to synchronous executions only; async executions always buffer, and so do executions with an ``Idempotency-Key`` when ``broker.idempotency.enabled`` is true. Off forces buffering everywhere.
stream_passthrough_enabled.title: Stream Passthrough Enabled

transfer_deadline_s.description: Total time (seconds) a streamed response body may take to transfer, so a steady trickle or a slow-draining client cannot hold an upstream connection forever; the stream is aborted when it is exceeded. Unlike ``read_timeout_s`` this bounds the whole body. 0 disables the deadline.
transfer_deadline_s.title: Transfer Deadline S

write_timeout_s.description: Per-write timeout (seconds) while sending a request body upstream.
write_timeout_s.title: Write Timeout S

UpstreamClientConfig.title: UpstreamClientConfig

VendorAuthConfig.description:
Config entry for one verified vendor.

Keyed in `VendorRegistryConfig.entries` by a short slug (e.g. "github").

display_name.description: Vendor name shown in the connect picker.
display_name.title: Display Name

flows.description: OAuth flows the vendor supports, selected by ``kind``. The first entry is used when the caller expresses no preference.
flows.title: Flows

identity_probe.description: Request that labels the connected account (``connected_as``) after a successful connect. Unset, the credential is still valid but carries no label.

scopes.description: The vendor's scope catalog offered on the review page.
scopes.title: Scopes

vendor.description: Catalog API id of the vendor's API, in ``<domain>/<name>`` form (e.g. ``github.com/api.github.com``); credentials created through this entry are scoped to it.
vendor.title: Vendor

VendorAuthConfig.title: VendorAuthConfig

VendorAuthorizationCodeFlowConfig.description:
OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow settings for a vendor.

Included so the vendor registry is flow-generic from day 1 even though
phase 1 only wires up device flow. Requires a client secret (confidential
client) since the redirect-based flow exchanges the code at the token
endpoint.

client_secret.description: OAuth application secret used to exchange the code at the token endpoint.
client_secret.title: Client Secret

VendorAuthorizationCodeFlowConfig.title: VendorAuthorizationCodeFlowConfig

VendorDeviceAuthorizationFlowConfig.description:
RFC 8628 device flow settings for a vendor.

`client_id` is the platform-shipped OAuth application id (device flow is a
public-client flow — no secret). Endpoints are the vendor's device
authorization + token endpoints.

authorization_endpoint.description: The vendor's device authorization endpoint URL.
authorization_endpoint.title: Authorization Endpoint

client_id.description: Platform-shipped OAuth application id (public client, no secret).
client_id.title: Client Id

VendorDeviceAuthorizationFlowConfig.title: VendorDeviceAuthorizationFlowConfig

VendorIdentityProbeConfig.description:
Generic identity-echo protocol config for a vendor.

After the connect flow completes, the platform calls
`{method} {endpoint}` with the freshly minted access token, extracts
`identity_field` (dotted JSON path) from the response body, and formats it
into `display_template` (Python str.format). The result is stored as
`connected_as` and returned to the caller.

display_template.description: Python ``str.format`` template for the ``connected_as`` label; it can reference top-level response fields and ``{value}`` (the extracted identity value).
display_template.title: Display Template

endpoint.description: URL called with the new access token to identify the connected account.
endpoint.title: Endpoint

identity_field.description: Dotted JSON path of the identity value in the probe response (e.g. ``login``).
identity_field.title: Identity Field

method.description: HTTP method of the identity probe.
method.title: Method

entries.description: Verified vendors offered by the agent-driven connect flow, keyed by a short slug (e.g. ``github``).
entries.title: Entries

VendorScopeConfig.description:
A single OAuth scope exposed by the vendor.

`classification` drives the review-page UX: read scopes are pre-selected by
default; write/admin scopes get a warning flag. `description` is
human-facing copy displayed on the review page.

classification.description: Risk class shown on the review page: write and admin scopes carry a warning.
classification.title: Classification

default.description: Pre-select this scope on the review page.
default.title: Default

description.description: Human-facing explanation of the scope, shown on the review page.
description.title: Description

name.description: Scope string as the vendor expects it on the authorize request.
name.title: Name

WorkerConfig.description:
Background job-worker durability knobs.

The worker claims a job, sets a **visibility deadline** (``visibility_timeout_s``
from claim), and processes it. A job left ``RUNNING`` past that deadline by a
crashed worker/pod is reclaimed on a later poll. A handler failure requeues the
job with capped exponential backoff up to ``max_attempts`` claims; beyond that
it is dead-lettered (poison-message handling) rather than looped forever. A
handler that raises ``NonRetryableJobError`` (a failure no retry can change,
such as an import whose spec fails validation) fails the job on that attempt
instead.

Each claim is a single atomic ``UPDATE`` (``FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`` on
Postgres, a serialised write transaction on SQLite), so any number of worker
loops — across processes or replicas, each running up to ``concurrency``
jobs — can poll the same queue without double-claiming a job.

concurrency.description: Maximum jobs one worker process runs at once (1 = serial). Postgres only: SQLite requires 1, because a job's handler holds the database write lock across its upstream call, so a second concurrent job's writes would time out. Each in-flight job holds about 2 admin-DB connections at once (its handler transaction plus the run-time authorization or credential-audit session it opens), so ``2 * concurrency`` must stay below ``databases.admin.pool_max``, leaving the remainder for HTTP requests and other background work in the same process.
concurrency.title: Concurrency

drain_timeout_s.description: On graceful shutdown, how long (seconds) the worker waits for in-flight jobs to finish. Past it the worker stops; a still-``RUNNING`` job is reclaimed via its visibility timeout after restart, so no work is dropped.
drain_timeout_s.title: Drain Timeout S

max_attempts.description: Total claims of a repeatedly failing job before it is dead-lettered instead of requeued.
max_attempts.title: Max Attempts

poll_interval_s.description: Idle wait (seconds) between job-queue polls when nothing is claimable. A job enqueued in the same process wakes the worker immediately, so this mainly bounds pickup latency for jobs enqueued by another process and how quickly visibility-expired jobs are reclaimed. Every poll is a write transaction (the claim is an ``UPDATE``) even when the queue is empty — on SQLite it takes the database write lock that request writes also wait on — so each process issues about ``1 / poll_interval_s`` of them per second while idle.
poll_interval_s.title: Poll Interval S

reconnect_backoff_base_s.description: First delay, in seconds, before the worker retries after losing its database connection. Doubles on each further failed attempt up to ``reconnect_backoff_max_s``; each delay is then jittered into the upper half of its value so workers sharing a database do not retry in lockstep.
reconnect_backoff_base_s.title: Reconnect Backoff Base S

reconnect_backoff_max_s.description: Cap, in seconds, on the worker's reconnect delay while the database is unreachable — a recovered database is picked up within this long.
reconnect_backoff_max_s.title: Reconnect Backoff Max S

retry_backoff_base_s.description: Base delay (seconds) before a failed job becomes claimable again: attempt ``n`` waits ``min(retry_backoff_base_s * 2**(n-1), retry_backoff_max_s)``.
retry_backoff_base_s.title: Retry Backoff Base S

retry_backoff_max_s.description: Cap (seconds) on the exponential backoff between attempts of a failed job.
retry_backoff_max_s.title: Retry Backoff Max S

sweep_interval_s.description: Seconds between the worker's retention sweeps, which expire lapsed execution approvals and delete expired job results and long-expired access/refresh token rows. Measured in wall time, independent of ``poll_interval_s`` and wake-ups.
sweep_interval_s.title: Sweep Interval S

visibility_timeout_s.description: Seconds a claimed (``RUNNING``) job stays invisible to other workers; past it the job is reclaimed and run again. Size it safely above the longest expected handler runtime (upstream timeout plus slack) so a healthy but slow job is never reclaimed mid-flight and processed twice.
visibility_timeout_s.title: Visibility Timeout S

WorkerConfig.title: WorkerConfig

apps.description: Surfaces this process serves: any of ``registry``, ``admin``, ``control``, ``auth``, or ``broker`` alone (the broker cannot be combined with other surfaces). Also decides which secrets production requires.
apps.title: Apps

state.description: The process's shared-state backend, built once and shared by every surface the process serves. The deprecated broker.resilience.backend section (and its JENTIC__BROKER__RESILIENCE__BACKEND__* env vars) is still read into it for one release.
